questions.question:
Which of the following airlines was nationalised in the 1953?

I. Bharat Airways

II. Hyderabad Aviation
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The civil aviation industry in India underwent a major transformation with the passage of the **Air Corporations Act** in **1953**, which led to the **nationalisation** of the entire sector.
 
• Under this **Act**, the **Government of India** decided to merge **eight** existing private airlines into two state-owned autonomous corporations.
 
• The eight airlines involved in the nationalisation process were **Air India**, **Air Services of India**, **Airways (India)**, **Bharat Airways**, **Deccan Airways**, **Himalayan Aviation**, **Indian National Airways**, and **Kalinga Airlines**.
 
• **Statement I**: **Bharat Airways** was one of the major private entities founded by the **Birla Group** in **1945**. It was indeed nationalised in **1953** as part of the merger to form **Indian Airlines**. ***Hence, statement I is correct.***
 
• **Statement II**: While **Deccan Airways** (based in Hyderabad) was nationalised, there was no major airline officially recognized as **"Hyderabad Aviation"** among the primary eight companies merged under the **1953 Act**. ***Hence, statement II is incorrect.***
 
• The merger resulted in the creation of **Indian Airlines Corporation** for domestic operations and **Air India International** for overseas services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Early History of Aviation**: **J.R.D. Tata**, often called the father of Indian civil aviation, launched **Tata Airlines** in **1932**, which carried mail between **Karachi** and **Bombay**. This company was renamed **Air India** in **1946**.
 
• **Bharat Airways**: Established by **G.D. Birla**, this airline was headquartered in **Calcutta** (now **Kolkata**). It played a significant role in providing air connectivity in the post-independence era before being absorbed into the public sector.
 
• **The Air Corporations Act, 1953**: This legislation was enacted to ensure the planned and coordinated development of air transport services. It gave the government a **monopoly** over the aviation sector for several decades.
 
• **Liberalization**: The monopoly created by the **1953 Act** lasted until **1994**, when the **Air Corporations (Transfer of Undertaking and Repeal) Act** was passed. This allowed private scheduled carriers like **Jet Airways** and **Sahara India** to enter the market again.
 
• **Modern Context**: In **January 2022**, the wheel of history came full circle when **Air India** was officially handed back to the **Tata Group**, marking the end of the era of nationalisation for the flagship carrier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The nationalisation was driven by the need for **financial stability** in the aviation industry, as many private airlines were struggling with high operating costs and low profit margins in the early **1950s**.
 
• The **Indian Airlines Corporation** initially took over the fleet of **74 Douglas DC-3 Dakotas**, **12 Vickers Vikings**, and other aircraft from the nationalised private companies.
 
• The headquarters of **Indian Airlines** was established in **New Delhi**, while **Air India** maintained its primary base in **Bombay** (now **Mumbai**).

questions.question: Who was the last ruler of Nanda dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dhana Nanda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dhana Nanda** was the **last ruler** of the **Nanda Dynasty**, which held power over the **Magadha** region in ancient India during the **4th century BCE**.
 
• He was the youngest of the **nine sons** of **Mahapadma Nanda**, who are collectively known in historical and religious texts as the **Navanandas**.
 
• During his reign, **Alexander the Great** invaded the north-western part of India in **326 BCE**. Historical accounts suggest that Alexander's army refused to cross the **Beas River** primarily due to the fear of **Dhana Nanda's** massive and formidable military force.
 
• His rule came to an end around **322–321 BCE** when he was defeated and **overthrown** by **Chandragupta Maurya**, who was assisted by the strategic brilliance of **Chanakya** (Kautilya).
 
• The downfall of **Dhana Nanda** marked the transition from the Nanda period to the **Mauryan Empire**, which eventually unified most of the Indian subcontinent.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahapadma Nanda**:

 
 
• He was the **founder** of the Nanda dynasty and is often regarded as the first **historical emperor** of India.
 
• In the **Puranas**, he is described as **"Sarva-Kshatrantaka"** (the uprooter of all Kshatriyas) and **"Ekarat"** (the sole monarch).
 
• He successfully expanded the **Magadhan Empire** by conquering various kingdoms like the **Kurus**, **Panchalas**, and **Kashis**.
 
 
 
• **The Nanda Military**:
 
 
• The dynasty was famous for its **military strength**. According to Greek historians like **Curtius**, the Nanda army consisted of **200,000 infantry**, **20,000 cavalry**, **2,000 chariots**, and **3,000 elephants**.
 
• This immense power ensured that **Magadha** remained the most dominant **Mahajanapada** of its time.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Social Conditions**:
 
 
• The name **"Dhana"** implies **wealth**. Ancient texts mention that the Nandas had accumulated **vast treasures** through a highly organized system of **taxation**.
 
• However, **Dhana Nanda** became highly **unpopular** among his subjects due to his **oppressive** tax regimes and his low-born status, which was looked down upon by the contemporary social elite.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Navanandas (The Nine Nandas)**:

 
 
• According to **Buddhist traditions** found in the **Mahabodhivamsa**, the nine kings were **Ugrasena** (Mahapadma Nanda), **Panduka**, **Pandugati**, **Bhuta-pala**, **Rashtra-pala**, **Govishanaka**, **Dashasiddhaka**, **Kaivarta**, and **Dhana Nanda**.
 
• They ruled for a relatively short duration, approximately **22 to 28 years**, but left a lasting impact on Indian administration.
 
 
 
• **Capital**:
 
 
• The **capital** of the Nanda Empire was **Pataliputra** (modern-day **Patna**). It was a major center for **trade**, **politics**, and **education**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chanakya**:
 
 
• The friction between **Chanakya** and **Dhana Nanda** is a significant historical theme. After being **insulted** in the Nanda court, Chanakya swore to destroy the dynasty and trained **Chandragupta Maurya** to fulfill this objective.

questions.question: The Vedic concept of 'kama' primarily relates to _____.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Desire and enjoyment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the **Vedic** tradition and broader **Hindu** philosophy, **Kama** is defined as one of the four **Puruṣārthas**, which are the legitimate goals of human life. It represents the pursuit of **desire**, **wish**, **passion**, and the **enjoyment** of life.
 
• The concept primarily relates to the **pleasure of the senses**, **aesthetic enjoyment** (such as art, music, and literature), **love**, and **affection**. It is not limited to physical desire but includes the emotional and psychological satisfaction derived from the world. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Kama** is considered an essential part of the human experience. However, it must be pursued within the framework of **Dharma** (ethical duty) to ensure that the pursuit of pleasure does not lead to social or personal harm.
 
• In the **Vedas**, the term is sometimes associated with the creative impulse of the universe. In the **Rigveda**, **Kama** is described as the "first seed of mind" that arose in the One during the creation of the cosmos.
 
• While **Ethical duties** refer to **Dharma**, **Selfless service** is more closely aligned with **Karma Yoga** or **Seva**, and **Detachment from worldly life** relates to **Vairagya** or **Sanyasa**. ***Hence, statements 1, 2, and 4 are incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The Four Puruṣārthas:**

 
 
• **Dharma (Duty):** This refers to **ethical duties**, **moral laws**, and **righteousness**. It is the foundation of the other three goals, ensuring that wealth and pleasure are acquired through **right conduct**.
 
• **Artha (Prosperity):** This signifies the pursuit of **material prosperity**, **wealth**, **economic values**, and **power**. It is necessary for maintaining a household and performing religious rituals.
 
• **Kama (Pleasure):** As discussed, it focuses on **desire and enjoyment**. It is the fulfillment of sensory and emotional needs during the **Grihastha** (householder) stage of life.
 
• **Moksha (Liberation):** This is the **ultimate goal** of human life, representing **spiritual liberation** and freedom from the cycle of birth and death (**Samsara**).
 
 
 
• **Kamasutra:**
 
 
• The most famous ancient Indian text on **Kama** is the **Kamasutra**, attributed to the sage **Vatsyayana**, believed to have been written between the **2nd and 4th century CE**.
 
• Far from being just a manual on physical love, it is a comprehensive guide to **social etiquette**, **aesthetic living**, and the **nature of love** and **relationships** in a civilized society.
 
 
 
• **The Ashrama System:**
 
 
• The pursuit of **Kama** is particularly emphasized in the **Grihastha** stage (householder stage) of the four **Ashramas**.
 
• During this stage, an individual is expected to get married, raise a family, and enjoy the **pleasures** of the world while fulfilling their **social** and **economic** obligations to society.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Deity of Kama:** In Indian mythology, **Kamadeva** is the god of **desire** and **attraction**, often depicted with a bow made of sugar cane and arrows decorated with five kinds of **fragrant flowers**.
 
• **Balance in Life:** Vedic philosophy warns against the excessive pursuit of **Kama** without **Dharma**, as it can lead to **greed** and **attachment**, which hinder the eventual path toward **Moksha**.
 
• **Upanishadic Perspective:** While the earlier **Vedic** texts recognize the importance of desire in creation, the **Upanishads** often emphasize transcending **desires** (**Kama**) to realize the **Atman** (Self) and achieve **peace**.

4f:T

questions.question: Which of the following is a characteristic of liquids?

options.text: No fixed shape but fixed volume
Fixed shape but no fixed volume
No fixed shape and no fixed volume

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**No fixed shape but fixed volume**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Liquids** are a state of matter characterized by having a **definite volume** but **no definite shape**. This means they will occupy the same amount of space regardless of the container, but will adapt their form to fit the bottom of that container. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• The particles in a **liquid** are **close together** with no regular arrangement. They vibrate, move about, and **slide past each other**, which allows liquids to **flow** and change shape.
 
• Unlike gases, the **intermolecular forces** in a liquid are strong enough to keep the particles in contact, ensuring a **fixed volume** that does not expand to fill the entire container.
 
• A **liquid** is nearly **incompressible**. Even under high **pressure**, the volume of a liquid decreases by a very small margin because the particles are already quite **packed**.
 
• When a liquid is poured into a vessel, it takes the **shape** of the part of the vessel it occupies due to **gravity** and the **fluidity** of its particles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Solids:**

 
 
• **Solids** possess a **fixed shape and a fixed volume**. The particles are **tightly packed** in a regular pattern and only **vibrate** around fixed positions. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• They have high **density** and are generally **rigid**, meaning they resist changes to their shape.
 
 
 
• **Gases:**
 
 
• **Gases** have **no fixed shape and no fixed volume**. The particles are far apart with **negligible attraction** between them, moving randomly at **high speeds**. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• A gas will **expand** to completely fill whatever **container** it is placed in, making it highly **compressible**.
 
 
 
• **Statement 3 Analysis:**
 
 
• The characteristic of having a **fixed shape but no fixed volume** does not correspond to any standard state of matter under normal conditions. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Physical Properties of Liquids:**
 
 
• **Viscosity:** This refers to a liquid's **resistance to flow**. For example, **honey** has a higher viscosity than **water** at **room temperature**.
 
• **Surface Tension:** This is the property of the **surface** of a liquid that allows it to resist an **external force**, due to the **cohesive** nature of its molecules. It is the reason why small insects can walk on water.
 
• **Boiling Point:** The **temperature** at which the **vapor pressure** of the liquid equals the **external pressure** surrounding the liquid, causing it to turn into a gas.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Diffusion:** Liquids undergo **diffusion**, where particles mix with other particles. The rate of diffusion in liquids is **higher** than in solids but **lower** than in gases.
 
• **Density:** Generally, the **density** of a substance in its **liquid state** is slightly lower than in its **solid state** (with the notable exception of **water**, where ice is less dense than liquid water).
 
• **Evaporation:** This is a **surface phenomenon** where liquid particles gain enough **kinetic energy** to escape into the **vapor phase** at temperatures below the boiling point.
 
• **Molecules in Motion:** The **kinetic energy** of liquid molecules is intermediate between that of solids and gases, allowing for **mobility** while maintaining **structural proximity**.

questions.question: During which occasion is the ‘Pathori Geet’ of Chhattisgarh traditionally sung?

options.text: Bidding farewell to a newly-wed bride

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bidding farewell to a newly-wed bride**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pathori Geet** is a traditional folk song belonging to the state of **Chhattisgarh**, primarily associated with the emotional rituals of marriage.
 
• This song is specifically performed during the **Vidaai** ceremony, which marks the occasion of **bidding farewell to a newly-wed bride** as she departs from her parental home to her husband's home.
 
• The theme of **Pathori Geet** is deeply melancholic, capturing the poignant moments of separation and the transition of a daughter into a new family. ***Hence, statement 4 is correct.***
 
• It is traditionally sung by the women of the family and the neighborhood, reflecting the socio-cultural values and the bond between a daughter and her **parents**.
 
• The lyrics often describe the path (**Path**) the bride is about to take and offer blessings for her future life, making it a vital part of the **Chhattisgarhi folk heritage**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Birth of a child:**

 
 
• The songs sung during the **birth of a child** in **Chhattisgarh** are known as **Sohar Geet**. These songs celebrate the arrival of the newborn and are filled with joy and hope. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Holi celebration:**
 
 
• During the **Holi celebration**, people sing **Phag Geet** or **Holi Geet**. These are energetic songs accompanied by instruments like the **Nagara** and **Mandar**, reflecting the spirit of colors and brotherhood. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Worship of Goddess Lakshmi:**
 
 
• The **Sua Geet** (Parrot Song) is performed during the **Deepawali** period, specifically during the **worship of Goddess Lakshmi** and **Gauri**. Women dance in a circle, mimicking the movement of a parrot. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Pandwani:**
 
 
• One of the most famous folk ballad forms of **Chhattisgarh** is **Pandwani**, which narrates the story of the **Pandavas** from the epic **Mahabharata**. Renowned artists like **Teejan Bai** have brought global recognition to this form.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dadariya:** Known as the **"King of Chhattisgarhi Folk Songs,"** it is a popular form of musical dialogue often sung during harvest or while performing daily tasks.
 
• **Karma Geet:** This is a tribal folk song performed during the **Karma Festival** by tribes such as the **Gonds**, **Baigas**, and **Oraons** to honor **Karam Sani**, the deity of destiny.
 
• **Panthi Geet:** Associated with the **Satnami** community of **Chhattisgarh**, these songs are performed to propagate the teachings and principles of **Guru Ghasidas**.
 
• **Bhartari:** A narrative folk song based on the legends of **King Bhartari**, usually sung with instruments like the **Iktara** and **Sarangi**.
 
• The state of **Chhattisgarh**, formed on **1st November 2000**, is often referred to as the **"Rice Bowl of India"** and possesses a rich tapestry of tribal art and oral traditions.

questions.question: As per NFHS-5, what percent of people living in urban areas live in households with electricity?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**99.1%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **National Family Health Survey-5 (NFHS-5)**, which was conducted between **2019 and 2021**, the percentage of households in **urban areas** with access to **electricity** is **99.1%**.
 
• The survey indicates a near-universal electrification in urban centers, reflecting the success of various urban development and power distribution schemes.
 
• For **rural areas**, the percentage of households with electricity access stands at **95.8%**, showing a significant catch-up with urban infrastructure.
 
• On a **national level**, the total percentage of households having access to electricity is **96.8%**, which is a substantial increase from the **88.2%** recorded during **NFHS-4 (2015-16)**.
 
• The **International Institute for Population Sciences (IIPS)**, Mumbai, served as the nodal agency for the survey under the aegis of the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Improved Drinking Water Sources**:

 
 
• In **NFHS-5**, **95.9%** of households in **India** have access to an improved source of drinking water.
 
• In **urban areas**, this figure is as high as **98.7%**, compared to **94.5%** in **rural areas**.
 
 
 
• **Sanitation Facilities**:
 
 
• Around **70.2%** of households in the country use **improved sanitation facilities** that are not shared with other households.
 
• There is a marked difference between regions, with **81.5%** in **urban areas** and **64.9%** in **rural areas** having access to such facilities.
 
 
 
• **Clean Cooking Fuel**:
 
 
• The use of **clean cooking fuel** (LPG/natural gas, biogas) stands at **58.6%** nationally.
 
• **Urban areas** lead significantly with **89.7%**, while **rural areas** lag behind at **43.2%** usage.
 
 
 
• **Housing Characteristics**:
 
 
• **96.7%** of **urban households** live in a "pucca" or semi-pucca structure, whereas the national average for households living in "pucca" houses has risen to **60.3%**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Scope of NFHS-5**: The survey provides high-quality data on **population, health, and nutrition** for **India** and each **State/Union Territory**. It covered approximately **6.37 lakh sample households** across the country.
 
• **Survey Phases**: The **NFHS-5** was conducted in two phases. **Phase I** covered 17 States and 5 UTs, while **Phase II** covered the remaining 11 States and 3 UTs.
 
• **Key Parameters**: Apart from household amenities, the survey tracks **Total Fertility Rate (TFR)**, which has declined to **2.0** at the national level, and **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)**.
 
• **Electricity Schemes**: The progress in electricity access is often attributed to the **Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana (Saubhagya)**, launched in **September 2017**, aimed at achieving universal household electrification.
 
• **State Performance**: Several states like **Goa, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu** reported nearly **100%** electricity access in both urban and rural sectors in this report.

questions.question: Who among the following was the Viceroy of India when Simon Commission came to India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Lord Irwin**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Lord Irwin** served as the **Viceroy of India** from **1926 to 1931**, a period marked by significant political upheaval and the rise of the independence movement.
 
• The **Simon Commission**, officially known as the **Indian Statutory Commission**, was appointed by the British government in **November 1927**.
 
• The commission arrived in **India** in **February 1928** at **Bombay** (now **Mumbai**) to review the working of the **Government of India Act 1919** and suggest further constitutional reforms.
 
• It was headed by **Sir John Simon** and consisted of **seven members** of the British Parliament, but notably, it did not include a single **Indian member**.
 
• The exclusion of Indians from a commission meant to decide India's constitutional future led to widespread outrage and a boycott by almost all Indian political parties, including the **Indian National Congress** and the **Muslim League**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Lord Chelmsford (1916–1921):**

 
 
• He was the **Viceroy** during the introduction of the **Montagu-Chelmsford Reforms** and the **Government of India Act 1919**.
 
• His tenure saw the infamous **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre** in **1919** and the launch of the **Non-Cooperation Movement** and **Khilafat Movement**.
 
 
 
• **Lord Willingdon (1931–1936):**
 
 
• He succeeded **Lord Irwin** and was the **Viceroy** during the **Second and Third Round Table Conferences**.
 
• The **Communal Award (1932)** and the **Government of India Act 1935** were significant landmarks during his administration.
 
 
 
• **Lord Linlithgow (1936–1944):**
 
 
• He served as **Viceroy** during the outbreak of **World War II** in **1939**.
 
• His tenure is noted for the **Quit India Movement (1942)**, the **August Offer (1940)**, and the **Cripps Mission (1942)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Simon Commission** was greeted with black flags and slogans of **"Simon Go Back"** across the country.
 
• During a protest in **Lahore** in **October 1928**, the veteran leader **Lala Lajpat Rai** was severely injured in a **lathi charge** and later succumbed to his injuries, which intensified the nationalist sentiment.
 
• As a response to the challenge by **Lord Birkenhead** (the Secretary of State) that Indians were incapable of drafting a constitution, the **Nehru Report** was prepared in **1928** under the chairmanship of **Motilal Nehru**.
 
• **Lord Irwin** later made the famous **Deepavali Declaration** in **October 1929**, stating that the natural issue of India's constitutional progress was the attainment of **Dominion Status**.
 
• His tenure also saw the **Dandi March (1930)** and the subsequent **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** signed on **March 5, 1931**, which led to the suspension of the **Civil Disobedience Movement**.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi started the famous Salt March accompanied by how many of his trusted volunteers?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**78**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi** initiated the historic **Salt March**, also known as the **Dandi March** or the **Salt Satyagraha**, on **12 March 1930**.
 
• The march began from **Sabarmati Ashram** in **Ahmedabad** and was destined for the coastal village of **Dandi** in **Gujarat**.
 
• Gandhi was accompanied by **78** of his trusted **volunteers** at the start of the journey. These individuals were meticulously chosen from different regions of **India** to represent a cross-section of the nation's **unity**.
 
• The marchers traversed a distance of approximately **240 miles** (about **385 kilometers**) over a period of **24 days**.
 
• The primary objective was to defy the **British salt monopoly** and the **Salt Tax**, which **Gandhi** viewed as an unjust burden on the **common people** and the **poor** of **India**.

__
 
• **The Symbolism of Salt**:

 
 
• **Salt** was selected as a symbol of **protest** because it was a commodity used by every household in **India**, regardless of **caste**, **creed**, or **economic status**.
 
• By choosing a universal necessity, **Gandhi** successfully mobilized the **masses** and bridged the gap between the **political elite** and the **rural population**.
 
 
 
• **Launch of Civil Disobedience**:
 
 
• The **Dandi March** marked the official beginning of the **Civil Disobedience Movement**, a major phase in the **Indian Independence Movement**.
 
• On **6 April 1930**, **Gandhi** reached **Dandi** and ceremonially broke the law by picking up a handful of natural salt from the shore, signifying the **non-violent** refusal to cooperate with the **British Raj**.
 
 
 
• **International Impact**:
 
 
• The march attracted significant **international media** attention. The **American journalist Webb Miller** provided detailed accounts of the movement, which helped shift **global opinion** in favor of **Indian self-rule**.
 
• It showcased the efficacy of **Satyagraha** (truth-force) and **Ahimsa** (non-violence) as powerful political tools against **colonialism**.

• The **British authorities** responded with a massive crackdown, arresting nearly **60,000** people, including **Mahatma Gandhi** and **Jawaharlal Nehru**.

• This culminated in the **Gandhi-Irwin Pact** signed in **March 1931**, which resulted in the release of **political prisoners** and allowed people living near the coast to produce salt for **personal consumption**.
 
 
 
• **Dharasana Satyagraha**:
 
 
• After **Gandhi's** arrest, **Sarojini Naidu** led a non-violent raid on the **Dharasana Salt Works** in **May 1930**, where peaceful protesters were brutally beaten by **British** police, an event that shocked the **world**.

questions.question: A sound wave has a frequency of 5 { kHz} and wave length 50 { cm} . How long (in seconds) will it take to travel 5 { km} ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• To find the time taken by the sound wave to travel a certain distance, we first need to determine the **speed of the sound wave** using the given **frequency** and **wavelength**.
 
• The **frequency (f)** of the sound wave is given as **5 kHz**. Converting this to the standard SI unit, **1 kHz = 1000 Hz**, thus the frequency is **5000 Hz**.
 
• The **wavelength (λ)** is given as **50 cm**. Converting this to meters (SI unit), **100 cm = 1 m**, so the wavelength is **0.5 m**.
 
• The **speed (v)** of a wave is calculated using the formula: **v = f × λ**. By substituting the values: **v = 5000 Hz × 0.5 m = 2500 m/s**.
 
• The **distance (d)** to be traveled is **5 km**. Converting this to meters, **1 km = 1000 m**, so the distance is **5000 m**.
 
• The **time (t)** taken is calculated using the formula: **t = distance / speed**. Substituting the values: **t = 5000 m / 2500 m/s = 2 seconds**. ***Hence, the time taken is 2 seconds.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Frequency:** It refers to the number of complete oscillations or cycles a wave makes per unit of time. The **SI unit** of frequency is the **Hertz (Hz)**, named after **Heinrich Hertz**. In this problem, the **high frequency** of **5000 Hz** indicates an ultrasonic or high-pitched sound.
 
• **Wavelength:** This is the **minimum distance** after which the sound wave repeats itself, typically measured between two consecutive **crests** or **compressions**. Its **SI unit** is the **meter (m)**.
 
• **Wave Speed:** The speed of sound depends on the **medium** through which it travels. In this calculation, the speed was found to be **2500 m/s**, which is significantly higher than the speed of sound in **air** (approximately **343 m/s** at **20°C**). This suggests the wave is likely traveling through a **solid** or a dense **liquid**, as sound travels fastest in **solids**.
 
• **Distance and Time:** The linear relationship between **distance**, **speed**, and **time** assumes that the wave speed remains **constant** throughout the journey. In real-world scenarios, factors like **temperature** and **humidity** can alter the speed of sound over a **5 km** stretch.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Unit Conversions:** It is crucial to convert all units to the **International System of Units (SI)** before performing calculations.

 
 
• **1 kilometer (km) = 1000 meters (m)**.
 
• **1 kilohertz (kHz) = 1000 hertz (Hz)**.
 
• **1 centimeter (cm) = 0.01 meters (m)**.
 
 
 
• **The Wave Equation:** The fundamental relation **v = fλ** applies to all types of waves, including **longitudinal sound waves** and **transverse light waves**.
 
• **Audible Range:** Human ears can typically hear sounds with frequencies between **20 Hz and 20,000 Hz (20 kHz)**. Since the frequency in the question is **5 kHz**, it falls well within the **audible range** for humans.

questions.question:

questions.question: In the context of LPG reforms in India, the growth of GDP increased from 5.6\% during 1980-1991 to ____ during 2007-2012 .
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**8.2%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The economic reforms in India, initiated in **1991**, are commonly known as the **LPG** (**Liberalization, Privatization, and Globalization**) reforms. These reforms were aimed at making the Indian economy more market-oriented and service-oriented.
 
• Before the implementation of these reforms, the Indian economy was characterized by slow growth, often referred to as the "Hindu Rate of Growth." During the period **1980-1991**, the **GDP** growth rate was approximately **5.6%**.
 
• Post-1991, the structural adjustments led to a significant boost in economic productivity. By the **11th Five Year Plan**, which spanned from **2007-2012**, the **GDP** growth rate increased to **8.2%**.
 
• This growth of **8.2%** during the **2007-2012** period is noteworthy because it was achieved despite the **Global Financial Crisis of 2008**, which slowed down economies worldwide.
 
• The shift in growth was primarily driven by the **Service Sector**, which grew at an average rate of nearly **10%** during the **11th Plan**, while the industrial sector also showed marked improvement compared to the pre-reform era.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background of 1991 Reforms**:

 
 
• India faced a severe **Balance of Payments (BOP)** crisis in **1991**, where **Foreign Exchange Reserves** dropped to a level that could only sustain about **two weeks** of imports.
 
• The government, led by Prime Minister **P.V. Narasimha Rao** and Finance Minister **Dr. Manmohan Singh**, approached the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** and the **World Bank** for a loan of **7 billion dollars**.
 
• In exchange for the loan, India agreed to liberalize its economy by reducing **tariffs**, removing the **License Raj**, and opening sectors to **Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)**.
 
 
 
• **LPG Components**:
 
 
• **Liberalization**: This involved the removal of government restrictions on private individual activities and the deregulation of industrial licensing.
 
• **Privatization**: It referred to the withdrawal of state ownership from public sector undertakings (PSUs) through **disinvestment**.
 
• **Globalization**: This aimed at integrating the Indian economy with the global economy through the free flow of **trade**, **capital**, and **technology** across borders.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact**:
 
 
• The reforms led to an increase in **Foreign Institutional Investment (FII)** and **FDI**, which rose from negligible amounts in the **1980s** to billions of dollars annually by the **2000s**.
 
• The **10th Five Year Plan (2002-2007)** had previously recorded a growth rate of **7.6%**, showing a steady upward trajectory leading into the **8.2%** achievement of the **11th Plan**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **11th Five Year Plan (2007-2012)** originally set a target of **9%** growth, but the actual achievement was **8.2%**. This was still considered a major success given the global economic downturn.
 
• One of the critical shortcomings during the high-growth phase of **2007-2012** was that the **Agriculture Sector** did not grow as fast as intended, hovering around **3.2%**, highlighting the "jobless growth" concern in some segments.
 
• The **Foreign Exchange Reserves** of India, which were roughly **1.2 billion dollars** in **June 1991**, climbed to over **290 billion dollars** by the end of the **11th Plan** in **March 2012**.
 
• The **Fiscal Deficit**, which was as high as **8.4%** of the **GDP** in **1990-91**, was subjected to stricter management through the **Fiscal Responsibility and Budget Management (FRBM) Act** of **2003**.

questions.question: In Football, the match lasts two equal periods of ____ minutes.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**45**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• According to the **Laws of the Game** established by the **International Football Association Board (IFAB)**, a standard professional football match lasts for a total duration of **90 minutes**.
 
• The match is strictly divided into **two equal periods** of **45 minutes** each. ***Hence, the correct answer is 45.***
 
• There is an interval between the two halves, commonly referred to as **half-time**, which must not exceed **15 minutes** as per standard regulations.
 
• The duration of each period may be reduced only if permitted by competition rules and if agreed upon by the **referee** and both participating teams before the match commences.
 
• The **referee** acts as the sole timekeeper on the field, ensuring that the full **45 minutes** of play are completed in each half, excluding any added time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Stoppage Time:** At the conclusion of each **45-minute** period, the referee adds **allowance for time lost**, also known as **stoppage time** or **injury time**. This accounts for **substitutions**, assessment/removal of **injured players**, **wasting time**, and **VAR** (Video Assistant Referee) reviews.
 
• **Extra Time:** In knockout formats where a winner must be decided, if the scores are level after the regulation **90 minutes**, the match proceeds to **extra time**. This consists of **two equal periods** of **15 minutes** each, totaling **30 minutes** of additional play.
 
• **The Field of Play:** A standard football pitch for international matches must have a length (touchline) of **100–110 meters** and a width (goal line) of **64–75 meters**.
 
• **Team Composition:** A match is played by two teams, each consisting of a maximum of **11 players**, one of whom is the **goalkeeper**. The minimum number of players required to maintain a match is **7** per team.
 
• **FIFA:** The **Federation Internationale de Football Association (FIFA)** is the global governing body that organizes major tournaments like the **FIFA World Cup**, which is held every **4 years**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:** The standard **90-minute** duration (two halves of **45 minutes**) was officially adopted in **1866** during a match between **London** and **Sheffield**, setting a precedent that was later codified into the universal laws.
 
• **The Ball:** A standard football (size 5) used in professional matches must have a circumference between **68 cm and 70 cm** and weigh between **410 g and 450 g** at the start of the game.
 
• **Disciplinary Actions:** During the **45-minute** periods, the referee has the authority to issue **yellow cards** (caution) and **red cards** (sending off) to players for fouls or misconduct.
 
• **Abandoned Matches:** If a match is abandoned before the completion of the **90 minutes** (two **45-minute** halves), it is usually replayed in full unless the competition rules state otherwise.

questions.question: Which of the following tomb is known for being entirely made of white marble?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Itimad-ud-daula's Tomb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The tomb of **Itimad-ud-daula** was commissioned by **Nur Jahan**, the wife of **Mughal Emperor Jahangir**, for her father **Mirza Ghiyas Beg**.
 
• Constructed between **1622 and 1628 AD**, it is located in **Agra** on the eastern bank of the **Yamuna River**.
 
• It holds the distinction of being the first **Mughal** structure built entirely of **white marble**, marking a significant departure from the **red sandstone** architecture dominant during **Akbar's** reign.
 
• The monument is often referred to as the **'Baby Taj'** because many of its architectural elements and the use of **Pietra Dura** (floral inlay work with semi-precious stones) served as a prototype for the **Taj Mahal**.
 
• The structure is situated within a classical **Charbagh** (four-quartered garden) layout and features **hexagonal towers** at each of its four corners.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agra Fort**:

 
 
• A **UNESCO World Heritage Site** rebuilt by **Emperor Akbar** in **1565** using **red sandstone**.
 
• It houses several notable buildings like the **Jahangiri Mahal**, **Moti Masjid**, and **Diwan-i-Aam**.
 
 
 
• **Akbar's Mausoleum**:
 
 
• Located at **Sikandra**, the construction was started by **Akbar** and completed by his son **Jahangir** in **1613**.
 
• The five-story structure is primarily made of **deep red sandstone**, though the top floor is constructed from **white marble**.
 
 
 
• **Jodha Bai's Tomb**:
 
 
• Built for **Mariam-uz-Zamani** (Jodha Bai), the mother of **Jahangir**, it is located near **Sikandra**.
 
• This tomb is constructed of **red sandstone** and features distinct **Mughal and Rajput** architectural styles.

questions.question: In April 2025, India ended the transshipment facility for which of the following neighbouring country for exports?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bangladesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• India discontinued the **transshipment facility** for **Bangladesh** in **April 2025**, which significantly affects how goods from the neighboring nation reach international markets via Indian territory.
 
• This facility previously allowed **Bangladeshi exporters** to use Indian **land ports**, **railways**, and **maritime ports** (such as **Kolkata** and **Haldia**) to ship goods to third countries, optimizing their **supply chain**.
 
• The cessation of these services impacts the **Indo-Bangla Protocol (IBP)** routes, which are vital for the movement of **bulk cargo** and **containers** between the two nations and beyond.
 
• Historically, the **transshipment** arrangement was a cornerstone of the **Economic Partnership**, aimed at reducing **logistics costs** and fostering regional connectivity under the **Neighborhood First Policy**.
 
• The move necessitates a shift in **Bangladesh's export strategy**, potentially increasing reliance on its own ports like **Chattogram** and **Mongla** for direct international shipping.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transshipment Mechanisms**:

 
 
• **Definition**: It involves the unloading of goods from one **ship** or **carrier** and loading them into another to complete a journey to a final destination.
 
• **Strategic Port**: The **Petrapole-Benapole** border remains the most critical land link, handling over **70 percent** of land-based trade between India and **Bangladesh**.
 
 
 
• **Economic Context**:
 
 
• **Bangladesh** is a major exporter of **Ready-Made Garments (RMG)**, and the loss of Indian transit routes adds pressure on their **delivery timelines** to **European** and **American** markets.
 
• The **South Asian Free Trade Area (SAFTA)** and the **BIMSTEC** framework have historically encouraged such transit facilities to boost **intra-regional trade**.

questions.question: Who received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2024 for chess?

• Gukesh played a pivotal role in leading the **Indian Men's team** to its first-ever **Gold Medal** at the **45th FIDE Chess Olympiad** in **Budapest**.
 
• His individual performance was equally stellar, securing an **Individual Gold Medal** on the top board with a staggering performance rating during the **Olympiad**.
 
• In **2023-2024**, he became the youngest player to cross the **2750 Elo rating** mark and briefly overtook **Vishwanathan Anand** as the top-ranked **Indian** player in the **FIDE** rankings.

• This is **India's** highest sporting honor, presented annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• It was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** before being renamed in **August 2021**.
 
• The award includes a medallion, a certificate, and a cash prize of **Rs. 25 lakh**.
